meta.description: The 306th Rescue Squadron Communications Shop provides reliable communications support for Guardian Angel operations. The team maintains and manages the communications equipment needed to keep personnel connected during training, exercises, and real-world missions. They also provide technical support, equipment accountability, and communications planning to ensure teams can effectively coordinate and accomplish the rescue mission.

meta.trafficSafetyNotes:
AFI 91-207 covers all traffic safety guidelines including motorcycle safety requirements.  This instruction applies to:
•	All AF military personnel at any time, on or off a DoD installation
•	All AF civilian personnel, on a DoD installation at any time, or in a duty status when off a DoD installation
•	All persons in or on an government owned or government leased/rented motor vehicle
•	All personnel at any time on an AF installation.  This includes all leased, owned, or privatized property.
Seat belts
Seat belt use is mandatory!  Seat belts, rollover protection systems (ROPS), airbags and other safety features are necessary for the safety of operators, passengers, bystanders, and the preservation of the equipment.  End users of Government Owned, Leased, Rented Vehicles, Government Vehicles Other (GVO), Government Off-Road Vehicles, Government Owned Recreational Motor Vehicles, (GORMVs) also known as Other Government Motor Vehicle Conveyances (OGMVC), will ensure applicable safety devices and features are installed, maintained and used. State law requires mandatory use of seat belts on and off base.
Helmets
All persons who ride a bicycle, tricycle or other human powered vehicle, including motorized bicycles, on an AF installation roadway, to include flight lines wear a properly fastened, approved (e.g., Consumer Product Safety Commission, American National Standards Institute, Snell Memorial Foundation or host nation equivalent) bicycle helmet. 
Speed limits
Off base
• Interstates & Freeways are typically 75 MPH i.e., Interstate 10
• Primary 4-lane divided highways 65 MPH
• Secondary 2-lane highways and county roads are 55 MPH
On Base
• Throughout - 30 mph unless otherwise posted
• Base housing – 15 mph unless otherwise posted
• Flight line - 5 mph near aircraft, no civilian vehicles allowed, no driving allowed without flight line validation on driver’s license.
Local traffic hazards
• Poor road quality i.e., potholes, lose or uneven shoulders:  Be aware of surface conditions and take added caution in areas of road construction.  Move to the opposite lane when you encounter vehicles stopped on the side of the road i.e., Arizona State law requires the driver to move to the left lane when encountering an emergency vehicle on the right shoulder, if unable to move over then driver will slow down and move to the left most part of the lane, passing with extreme caution.
• Weather conditions: Low lying roadways are prone to flooding and this area and subject to flash floods.  Slow down at night! With limited sight distance, comes limited reaction time.  Expect icy conditions on bridges, overpasses, and shaded areas during colder months when it rain, snow or freezes happen.  Dust storms do occur at times in Tucson and in between Tucson and Phoenix.  If you are caught in a dust storm and are able to pull to the side of the road turn off your lights, set park brake and keep foot off of brake.  If unable to pull off to the side of the road, reduce speed and proceed with caution.
• Animal/Object Strikes: Coyotes and Javelina are mostly the largest animals you will encounter crossing roadways in the Tucson area.  In the outer parts of Tucson the roads go through open ranges which are where you may encounter a cow along the side of the road or in the road.  If you see a coyote or Javelina or other large animal, SLOW DOWN and attempt to drive by the animal in a controlled manner.  Attempting to steer around objects at high speed causes many other issues that can cause the driver to lose control i.e., running off the roadway, uncontrolled spin, roll over.
Spotters
Spotters will be required when operator visibility is obscured or in question, when backing a vehicle, and prior to beginning aircraft up/downloading (with pre-positioned chock in place).  Backing of government-owned motor vehicles and the usage of spotters will be IAW AFMAN 24-306.
• Spotter(s) will use the following safety items during hours of darkness or periods of reduced visibility: reflective belt and flashlight or luminous wands.
• Spotter(s) must be trained in standard hand and arm signals and flashlight signals before guiding a vehicle
• Spotter(s) will position themselves away from the vehicle's path of travel and maintain visual contact with the vehicle operator.
• Government-owned motor vehicle operators will immediately stop if they lose visual contact with the spotter or notice the spotter is dangerously positioned between the vehicle and another object. In such cases, vehicle operators will secure the vehicle, exit and make an on-the-spot correction before continuing operations.
Licensing/Training requirements
• State driver’s license required to operate any vehicle.
• Certificate of Competency required for flight line driving and operation must be IAW AFI 13-213.
• Polaris Ranger/Razor, Utility Vehicles and other similar vehicles
	Before operating, personnel must complete the LSV/OGMV training.  
*See LSV/OGMV Power Points or click HERE
Use of electronic devices
• Unless a hands-free device is used, use of cell phone is prohibited while operating a vehicle on base.
• Federal employees shall not engage in text messaging (a) when driving GMV, or when driving PMV while on official Government business, or (b) when using electronic equipment supplied by the Government while driving.
• Arizona law prohibits drivers from using a cellphone or a stand-alone electronic device while driving unless it is being used in a hands-free mode. This includes, but is not limited to, cell phones, tablets, and music & gaming devices.
Motorcycles
AFI 91-207 has established policies on Motorcycle safety.  
• All military (both novice and experienced) must complete Motorcycle Safety Foundation (MSF) courses IAW AFI 91-207.
• All others (retirees, contractors, dependents, and civilians) who operate a motorcycle while on an AF installation are encouraged to complete a MSF course.
• All motorcycle riders will be briefed (initially and annually) by their Commander or designated representative on the requirements of motorcycle safety as outlined in AFI 91-207 and local policies. 
• All motorcycle riders must input there motorcycle information into the MUSTT system for tracking purposes.  Information needed will include: experience, certificate of training, year, make, model, engine size, etc. 
• All motorcycle riders will wear appropriate PPE to include helmet, eye protection, protective clothing and foot protection.
PT (jogging/running/walking/biking)
• The preferred PT areas on base are at the designated running tracks.  If this option is chosen, headphones are permitted and reflective material is not required while on the track.
• While performing PT on roadways:
	Headphones are not permitted to be worn
	Reflective clothing or gear  must be worn during hours of darkness or periods of reduced visibility 
	Personnel will PT against traffic
Other important information
• All vehicles must be insured to the state mandated level of liability.
• Park only in designated parking spots.
• Always yield to runners, walkers and bicyclists.
